title: Dogfood the orchestrator on its own downstream work
body: Plan 2026-05-09-003 just closed; the orchestrator now has the substrate to consume its own state-projection output. Rather than hand-code plans 010 + 004, drive them through supervisor.dispatch_volley and treat every terminal-non-success as signal for orchestrator improvement. Convention follows the harness_frictions_v1/v2 pattern from memory: real volleys surface real frictions; clustered findings get promoted to v3 fixes plan. Parent meta-plan structure follows nested-orchestration v1 (plan 2026-05-02-003): children declare orchestration block pointing up to this parent; parent is a regular plan that gets pointed at. spawn_reason: operator_manual on both children (operator deliberately authored both as downstream work after plan 003 closed).

title: Plan 004 goal_type new_feature → infra (avoid objective_contract overhead)
body: Plan 004 is adapter wiring on top of the state-projection contract shipped by plan 003. It does not introduce a new user-facing surface — the dashboard already exists in axiom/packages/dashboard/. Treating it as infra avoids the Goal Governance V1 objective_contract document requirement at lock time. Same framing as plan 010 (printing-press-adapter skill) and plan 003 (state-projection v0).

title: Plan 010 + plan 004 amended with child orchestration blocks (locked-plan metadata addition is structural, not scope)
body: Plan 010 was already status:active when this parent was drafted. Adding the orchestration + child_charter + commit_policy blocks to its plan.md frontmatter is metadata, not a change to the locked AC (features.json + acceptance text untouched). Per the scope-change protocol: explicitly flagged that locked frontmatter was edited; locked behavioral contract preserved. Plan 004 was draft so its frontmatter is freely editable. Both children now declare parent_plan_id = 2026-05-11-001-infra-state-projection-adapters-meta with spawn_reason: operator_manual.

title: FINDING (configuration-drift): quota_caps.json missing entries for active vendor windows
body: 3 startup warnings: (1) claude.rolling_7d calibration stale — requires `calibrate-claude` re-run; (2) claude.max_20x.rolling_5h has 12.7M weighted_tokens signal but NO cap entry; (3) codex.plus.rolling_7d has 574M tokens signal but NO cap entry. Volley proceeded anyway (ratio fallback). CLASSIFICATION: spec-clarification — config docs should tell operator which cap entries are required for each active vendor/window pair. Future v3 candidate: a `dontpanic doctor` quota check that surfaces missing-cap-entry vendor/window pairs as actionable warnings instead of buried-in-stderr.

title: FINDING (already-known + interpretive-disagreement?): iteration 0 audit verdict needs_changes — implementer + auditor disagree
body: Volley 1 iteration 0: claude (implementer) signed_off after writing 3 skill files; codex (auditor) returned needs_changes with 3 findings, including 'medium security: ADAPTER_TEMPLATE.md does not implement required sanitization checks on tool responses'. Cross-vendor audit caught a real gap. Tokens: claude 2.48M in / 22.8K out; codex 832K in / 12.9K out. CLASSIFICATION pending iteration 1 outcome: if iteration 1 resolves the security finding, this is a feature_defect surfaced by audit (good — system working as designed). If audit insists on the same finding after iteration 1 fix attempt, that's interpretive_disagreement worth investigating.

title: FINDING (feature_defect-candidate): implementer token cost surprise — 2.48M input on a docs-only feature
body: Iteration 0 implementer consumed 2.48M input tokens for a feature whose work was 'write 3 markdown files'. Output was 22.8K. The 100:1 input:output ratio suggests significant context bloat in the implementer prompt template — likely the full plan + features + all prior history + relevant skill context. For docs-heavy features this may be over-feeding. CLASSIFICATION: feature_defect-candidate. NEXT: measure iteration 1's token cost; if still 2M+ on a re-implement that should have less new context, prompt-template trimming becomes a real v3 candidate.

CLASSIFICATION: spec-clarification → v3 candidate. v3 plan F003 adds spec_ambiguity class to bridge this gap.

title: FINDING (feature_defect, amplified): v3 F001 token cost REGRESSED vs plan 010 baseline
body: v3 F001 total: 8.86M in / 63K out / 140:1 ratio. Plan 010 F001 baseline: 6.84M in / 68K out / 100:1 ratio. iter0 implementer alone consumed 4.92M tokens for a single check function + 9 tests. This AMPLIFIES the D007 signal — the prompt-template bloat is even worse than first measured. v3 F002 (implementer prompt-template trim) becomes higher priority. New target should be re-baselined from this run: from 4.92M iter0 → <1.5M iter0 (70% reduction, not 50%).
